- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 10–20%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3.0), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 2.5–3.0 for next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model underestimates; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for next 5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates true outcomes in early horizon (1–5 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply +0.1 to +0.4 adjustment for first 3 days.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags; forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
- For long-term (15+ days) forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth out extreme highs/lows by 10–15% unless sentiment confirms breakout.
